title: proxy-ingress-egress-fuzz-study-oct-2024
summary: Exploratory fuzzing of ingress->proxy->edge->backend interactions to find brittle pacing heuristics and microburst amplification. Goal: produce reproducible signal for heuristic fixes and a lightweight detection rule set.
content:
Purpose:
- Rapidly explore combinations of client chunking patterns, small/large payload mixes, TCP delayed-ACK/Nagle toggles, and chained proxy buffering to discover failure modes that surface as tail-latency or throughput collapse.
- Produce candidate heuristics (detection & mitigation) for the ingress proxy and edge egress path.

Why fuzzing?
- Deterministic benchmarks cover common cases but miss combinatorial interactions (e.g., small chunk sequences + intermittent client flush + backend KV warmup).
- We hypothesize many tail events are high-dimensional and triggered by rare sequences; fuzzing surfaces these.

Environment/setup (short):
- Cluster: 8-node perf cluster (g4dn.12x equivalent).
- Serving runtime: commit 4d2a7b (runtime binary with per-request pacing hooks enabled).
- Proxies: nginx-like edge (TCP level buffering) + internal multiplexing proxy (HTTP/2) + a small TCP reverse-proxy shim we control.
- Models: small LLM stub that emits 5..200 token responses deterministically (to control server-side compute noise).
- Workload generator: custom fuzz harness (python + asyncio) that emits randomized chunk sequences (configurable distributions), plus TCP options toggles.
- Measurement: per-request timeline with timestamps at client write, proxy accept, backend receive, backend first byte, backend end, proxy egress, client read complete. Additional counters: TLS handshake times, conn reuse counts, socket-level write sizes.

Fuzz space sampled (high level):
- Chunk size distribution: {single-byte spikes, 64B, 512B, 4KB} sampled with Zipf/Poisson mixes.
- Inter-chunk gaps: 0..500ms, heavy tail.
- Request concurrency: 1..64 (steady-state + burst windows).
- Keepalive patterns: frequent conn re-use vs new connections per request.
- Protocol variants: HTTP/1.1 chunked w/keepalive, HTTP/2 multiplexed, gRPC over HTTP/2 (with small messages).
- TCP options: Nagle on/off, delayed-ACK simulated toggles (via client OS and a tunable shim).

Key discoveries (reproducible patterns):
1) Microburst amplification via ingress buffering + HTTP/2 multiplexing
- Pattern: Many clients send many tiny chunks (1–8B) in quick succession but grouped per connection. Edge proxy coalesces a small window, then internal multiplexing sends frames that trigger internal scheduling spikes.
- Symptom: sudden 20–40x tail increase on a subset (~5%) of requests when concurrency > 16.
- Root cause sketch: coalescing window interacts with runtime batching thresholds; KV cache misses (cold lines) then amplify CPU stalls and cause egress stalls.

2) Delayed-ACK-ish interactions with intermittent flushes
- Pattern: clients send a small header packet then pause ~40–80ms then flush body.
- Symptom: long server-side stalls waiting for first body bytes; when combined with conn re-use the next request sees head-of-line egress delay.
- Note: behavior reproduced both with Nagle enabled and when simulated delayed ACKs were toggled in the kernel shim.

3) Proxy chain memory-pressure backpressure that looks like a throughput collapse
- Pattern: intermediate proxy enqueues many small requests during a short burst; memory limit triggers drop/slow-path where the proxy starts batching to reduce syscalls.
- Symptom: client sees partial streaming followed by long silence (~200–800ms) and then a burst of remaining bytes.
- Observed on both HTTP/1.1 chunking and HTTP/2; more severe on the HTTP/1.1 chain when the edge proxy rewrites chunk boundaries.

4) Conn reuse + stale KV cache correlation
- Pattern: long-lived connections that serve varied prompt sizes cause KV cache warm/cold churn in the runtime.
- Symptom: requests following a large generation sometimes hit higher latency if they reuse the same connection and the runtime reclaims/warms the KV cache.

Representative experiment (repro steps):
- Harness seed: 20241012-psi-07 (attached to linked artifacts PR).
- Start 64 concurrent clients, each opens 4 connections, producing small-chunk heavy Zipf distribution (1–16B, mode 4B) with inter-chunk gaps sampled Erlang(k=2, mean=15ms), then occasional 60ms pauses injected.
- Run 10k requests. Capture timelines.
- Outcome: 4.7% of requests had >150ms tail (p99.9) vs baseline 1.1%. Reproduced across 3 clusters with same seed.

Telemetry signals to add (detection rules):
- Spike in "first-byte delay" where backend-first-byte - proxy-accept > 30ms and is correlated with many small writes after TCP-level zero window events.
- Elevated syscall batching count / proxy coalesce events per second.
- Memory-watermark-triggered batching counters in proxy logs.
- Connection-level sequence: many tiny writes followed by silence.

Mitigations evaluated (quick notes):
- Ingress: reduce coalescing window under small-chunk heavy connections (adaptive window based on observed chunk size distribution). Quick win but increases syscall overhead.
- Runtime: prefer early KV prefetch for connections with recent large responses (heuristic: last response token count > 128) to avoid cold miss spikes. Reduced tail in our experiments by ~30%.
- Proxy: soft-drop microburst tail by applying per-conn pacing when queue depth exceeds threshold (emulate TCP pacing at app level). Prevented amplification but increased median by ~5–8ms.
- Client-side guidance: prefer slightly larger flush sizes (>=64B) and avoid 40–80ms pause patterns. We cannot control all clients but document as best-practice in SDKs.

Tradeoffs and costs:
- Smaller coalescing window -> more syscalls -> higher median CPU and cost.
- Pre-warming KV -> slightly higher memory usage and wasted prefetch cycles for benign patterns.
- App-level pacing -> smoother tails but modest latency/regression on median; acceptable for high-SLA tiers only.

Actionable next steps (short list):
- (A) Implement adaptive coalescing threshold toggle behind runtime feature flag. Run A/B for 2 weeks on dev-Dedicated pool. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 3w.
- (B) Add detection rule to alert on first-byte-delay spike correlated with small-write sequences. Owner: Lina. ETA: 1w.
- (C) Prototype KV prefetch heuristic and benchmark memory tradeoffs under realistic prompt distributions. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2w.
- (D) Add fuzz harness seed corpus to CI (deterministic seeds that previously reproduced amplification). Owner: Carlos. ETA: 1w.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How does real LLM compute jitter (non-stub) change amplification? need to run with actual 7B model container to validate.
- Interplay with TLS record coalescing at kernel: we simulated but need kernel-level traces from a customer case.
- Long-term: can we push a pacing primitive down to edge libproxy to avoid syscall cost? feasibility TBD with infra team.

Notes to self / quick log:
- Observed that HTTP/2 multiplexing shifts which requests get hit (not necessarily the oldest). Need deeper trace-level mapping.
- Some seeds only fail on specific kernel versions (observed on Ubuntu 20.04 vs 22.04). Capture kernel+tcp-tuning in debug runs.

Appendix (short):
- Harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-fuzz (PR linked).
- Raw experiment IDs: exp-20241012-psi-07, exp-20241015-mu-02, exp-20241020-kappa-01.
- Quick checklist for reproduction: ensure same runtime commit, proxy image, and kernel tunables; run harness seed and collect timeline trace.

End of notes.
